title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: British braised lamb mince under a golden mashed potato crust
excerpt: Shepherd's pie is one of the most beloved dishes in British cooking: braised lamb mince with carrots, onions, and a rich gravy, topped with a thick crust of creamy mashed potato and baked until golden. The name refers to the shepherd who tends the sheep -- when beef is used instead of lamb, it is correctly called cottage pie.
sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie has been made in Britain since the late 18th century. It was created as a way of using leftover roast meat with a potato topping -- potatoes being cheap and filling. The distinction between shepherd's pie (lamb) and cottage pie (beef) was established in the 19th century. The dish is eaten across Britain as a staple family meal.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before the final bake. Defrost completely before baking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 2 days ahead. Refrigerate and bake when needed.

content.text: The mince filling should be saucy -- not swimming in liquid, but with enough gravy to keep it moist under the potato. A dry filling becomes chalky. The mashed potato topping needs to be thick and stiff enough to support itself when spread over the filling. A very wet mash will sink into the meat rather than form a crust.

Heat a large frying pan over high heat. Brown {{lamb-mince}} lamb mince in two batches until well coloured. Remove and set aside. Reduce heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion and {{carrots}} carrots to the pan and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic, {{rosemary}} rosemary, and {{thyme-fresh}} thyme.

Return the mince. Add {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree, {{worcestershire-sauce}} Worcestershire sauce, and {{lamb-stock}} stock. Simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick. Add {{peas-frozen}} peas in the last 3 minutes. Season well.
Meanwhile, boil {{potatoes-floury}} potatoes until tender. Drain and mash with {{unsalted-butter}} butter, warm {{whole-milk}} milk, and {{salt-table}} salt until smooth.

Preheat the oven to 200C. Transfer the mince filling to a large ovenproof dish. Spoon the mash over the top and spread evenly. Run a fork across the surface to create ridges. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The mash has sunk into the meat rather than forming a crust
items.cause: The mash was too wet or too warm when it was spread.
items.fix: Make a stiffer mash next time -- use less milk. Let the filling cool slightly before adding the mash. A hot filling melts a warm mash and they blend together rather than staying separate.

content.text: Shepherd's pie is one of the most widely eaten dishes in Britain. It is a standard school dinner, a pub staple, a family supper, and a comfort food. The dish is made across the whole country in countless variations -- some add Worcestershire sauce, some add red wine, some finish the mash with cheese. The core of the dish -- braised mince under mashed potato -- is fixed.
